scams.name: Timeshare Presentation Trap
scams.description: A couple landed at Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport and before they even reached the exit doors, a man in a polo shirt with a resort lanyard intercepted them near the luggage carousel. He offered a 'free' all-inclusive dinner and discounted whale-watching tour — all they had to do was attend a 'quick 90-minute presentation' the next morning. They agreed, thinking they could easily say no. The presentation lasted over six hours. Multiple salespeople tag-teamed them with emotional manipulation, fake countdown timers on 'today-only' pricing, and veiled threats that declining would forfeit their dinner voucher. They signed a $18,000 timeshare contract under extreme pressure. The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned the CJNG cartel-linked Kovay Gardens resort near Puerto Vallarta in 2026 for running exactly this kind of operation — a vertically integrated fraud factory generating over $330 million in suspicious transactions, with victims' contact information sold to boiler-room call centers for repeated re-scamming. Forum posts on r/puertovallarta and TripAdvisor warn about this constantly, with the airport, the Malecón boardwalk, and resort lobbies being the primary hunting grounds.
scams.avoidance: Walk straight through the airport arrivals to your pre-booked transportation without stopping for anyone Pre-book airport transfers through your hotel or a verified service before you fly in Say 'No gracias' once and keep walking — do not engage, explain, or accept anything 'free' If you accidentally sign a timeshare contract, Mexican law gives you 5 business days to cancel in writing — document everything immediately Report timeshare fraud to PROFECO (Mexico's consumer protection agency) at 800-468-8722 or the FBI's IC3 at ic3.gov
scams.location: PVR Airport arrivals hall, Malecón boardwalk, resort lobbies, tequila shops along the Malecón

scams.name: Taxi Fare Inflation
scams.description: A solo traveler stepped out of her hotel in the Zona Romántica and flagged down a yellow taxi to get to Marina Vallarta — about a 15-minute ride. The driver quoted 350 pesos. She didn't know the going rate, so she agreed. At Marina Vallarta, a local friend told her the ride should have been 120-150 pesos maximum. The next day she took a taxi from the airport to her hotel in the Hotel Zone and was quoted $45 USD — roughly triple the authorized zone rate of around 250-300 pesos. Puerto Vallarta taxis have no meters, which means every fare is negotiated. Drivers on TripAdvisor and travel forums are consistently reported quoting tourists 2-3x the correct fare, knowing visitors have no reference point. Some drivers also take longer routes, or claim they cannot make change for large bills, pocketing the difference. Uber operates in Puerto Vallarta but faces periodic pushback from the taxi union, and some drivers have been harassed — so rides occasionally get cancelled.
scams.avoidance: Ask your hotel front desk what the correct taxi fare should be before you leave — they often have printed zone rate cards Always agree on the exact fare in pesos before getting into the taxi and confirm by saying the number aloud Use Uber or InDriver as an alternative — the app locks in the price so there is no room for negotiation games For airport transfers, buy an official taxi voucher at the authorized transportation desk inside the terminal before exiting Carry small bills in pesos (50s and 100s) so the driver cannot claim he has no change for a 500-peso note
scams.location: PVR Airport exits, Zona Romántica, Malecón, Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera)

scams.name: ATM Skimming & Card Swap
scams.description: A traveler used a standalone ATM inside an OXXO convenience store near the Malecón to withdraw 5,000 pesos. The machine worked normally and dispensed the cash. Four days later, back home in Texas, he discovered $3,200 in unauthorized withdrawals from his checking account. A skimming device had been installed on the ATM's card slot, and a pinhole camera above the keypad had recorded his PIN. In a separate incident reported on TripAdvisor forums, a woman's card got stuck in an ATM near Playa de los Muertos. A 'helpful' man appeared immediately and offered to assist, suggesting she enter her PIN again while he manipulated the machine. After she left to find her bank, she realized the man had swapped her card for a dummy — he now had both her real card and her PIN. Police in Puerto Vallarta have caught members of Romanian-led skimming gangs red-handed installing devices on ATMs in the Riviera Nayarit and Puerto Vallarta tourist zones.
scams.avoidance: Only use ATMs located inside bank branches (BBVA, Santander, Scotiabank, Banorte) during business hours — never use standalone ATMs in convenience stores, on streets, or in bars Before inserting your card, wiggle the card reader and check for loose parts, bulky housings, or pinholes above the keypad Always shield your PIN entry with your other hand — even inside a bank If your card gets stuck or the machine behaves oddly, cancel immediately, leave, and call your bank — never accept help from strangers When the ATM offers to convert to your home currency (DCC), always decline and choose pesos — declining saves you 5-10% in hidden conversion fees
scams.location: Standalone ATMs near Malecón, OXXO convenience stores, Zona Romántica side streets

scams.name: Mustard / Sauce Distraction Theft
scams.description: A couple was walking along the Malecón when a man bumped into them from behind, apparently by accident, and apologized in Spanish. The woman noticed a large smear of yellowish sauce on the back of her husband's shirt. Another person appeared almost immediately, pointing at the stain and offering napkins to help clean it off. While both of them were focused on the mess — the husband turning to look over his shoulder, the wife dabbing at his back — a third accomplice lifted the husband's phone from his front pocket and the wife's crossbody bag was unzipped. They didn't realize anything was missing until ten minutes later. This is known locally as the 'mustard scam' and is the most frequently reported street scam in Puerto Vallarta and nearby Bucerias. Variations use BBQ sauce, salsa, or even bird droppings (sometimes fake). It has been reported happening on the street, in Walmart parking lots, and even inside big-box stores. Multiple TripAdvisor and Reddit threads document this scam in detail.
scams.avoidance: If someone spills anything on you, immediately clutch your belongings and walk away — do not stop to clean up Do not accept help from strangers who appear conveniently after something is spilled on you Wear a money belt or keep your phone in a zipped interior pocket, especially on the Malecón and crowded streets Be extra alert when walking in pairs — the scam specifically exploits the moment both partners are distracted If you spot the stain trick in progress, loudly say 'No, gracias' and move to a well-lit, populated area before assessing damage
scams.location: Malecón boardwalk, Bucerias, Walmart and commercial parking lots, busy pedestrian streets in Centro

scams.name: Restaurant Bill Padding
scams.description: A group of friends sat down at a beachfront restaurant near Playa de los Muertos and ordered from a menu with reasonable prices — fish tacos at 180 pesos, margaritas at 120 pesos. The food was good and they relaxed. When the bill arrived, it was nearly double what they expected. Two rounds of chips and salsa they never ordered were charged at 90 pesos each. The margaritas were listed at 180 pesos instead of 120. When they asked to see the menu again, the waiter brought a different version with higher prices and insisted these were always the correct prices. In another well-documented variant on TripAdvisor forums, a waiter took a guest's cash payment folder containing a 500-peso note and returned claiming the guest had only given a 50-peso note — the bills look remarkably similar — requesting an additional 450 pesos. Some restaurants also bury a 15-18% automatic gratuity in very small print at the bottom of the bill, hoping tourists will tip an additional 15-20% on top without noticing.
scams.avoidance: Photograph the menu with your phone before ordering — this is your proof if prices change on the bill Review the itemized bill line by line before paying and question any item you did not order Check the bottom of the bill carefully for a 'propina' or 'servicio' line — if gratuity is already included, do not double-tip When paying cash, announce the denomination aloud as you hand it over ('quinientos pesos') and wait for the server to confirm before they walk away Pay with a credit card when possible for a transaction record, but always verify the peso amount on the terminal before approving
scams.location: Beachfront restaurants near Playa de los Muertos, tourist-facing restaurants on the Malecón, Zona Romántica dining strip

scams.name: Free Tequila Tasting Bait
scams.description: A young couple was strolling the Malecón when an enthusiastic man outside a tequila shop waved them over for a 'free tequila tasting — no obligation.' Inside, the shop was beautiful, the tequila was excellent, and after four or five generous pours they were feeling great. Then the conversation shifted. The 'tequila expert' asked where they were staying and casually mentioned that the shop's sister company offered an incredible private beach club experience — all they had to do was attend a short presentation tomorrow morning. It was a timeshare pitch disguised as a tequila tasting. In a more direct version reported on TripAdvisor, shops on the Malecón employ attractive staff who pour liberally, then steer tipsy tourists toward purchasing massively overpriced bottles of tequila — $200 USD for bottles that retail for $30 in any Guadalajara liquor store. Some shops also sell counterfeit 'premium' tequila in authentic-looking bottles. Multiple Puerto Vallarta forum posts warn that not every tequila shop on the Malecón is a front, but the ones with the most aggressive sidewalk promoters almost always have an ulterior motive.
scams.avoidance: Enjoy tequila tastings but exit immediately if anyone mentions a 'presentation,' 'meeting,' or 'exclusive experience' — these are timeshare code words Limit your intake during free tastings so you stay sharp enough to recognize sales tactics Check tequila prices on MercadoLibre or Amazon Mexico before buying — a bottle of good reposado should cost 400-800 pesos, not $150+ USD Buy tequila from established shops with strong Google reviews, or from Soriana and La Europea liquor stores where prices are fixed and transparent If a shop employee follows you out onto the sidewalk after you leave, do not re-engage — they are working on commission
scams.location: Tequila shops along the Malecón boardwalk, Centro Histórico, cruise ship terminal area

scams.name: Gas Station Pump Scam
scams.description: A tourist who rented a car to drive to Sayulita pulled into a Pemex gas station on Highway 200 north of Puerto Vallarta and asked the attendant to fill up with 500 pesos of magna. She handed over a 500-peso note. The attendant palmed it and then held up a 50-peso note — which looks very similar in color and size — insisting that was all she had given him. She was certain she had handed over 500 but had no proof, and ended up paying the difference of 450 pesos. In another common variant, the attendant does not reset the pump to zero before beginning to fill, so the meter starts at the previous customer's total and you end up being charged for gas you never received. Some stations also pump from a hose connected to the unit behind your car so you cannot see the running total. Travelers on TripAdvisor's Puerto Vallarta forum have documented these pump scams at multiple stations along the highway between PVR Airport and Nuevo Vallarta.
scams.avoidance: Before the attendant starts pumping, get out and verify the pump reads zero — point at it and say 'cero, por favor' Pay exclusively with 200-peso notes instead of 500s — the two denominations look nothing alike, eliminating the bill-switch trick Announce the bill denomination aloud as you hand it to the attendant: 'Quinientos pesos' while making eye contact Watch the pump display from your window throughout the entire fill-up — do not look at your phone Use Google Maps to find well-reviewed Pemex stations with consistent ratings rather than stopping at the first one you see
scams.location: Pemex stations on Highway 200 (PVR to Nuevo Vallarta/Sayulita corridor), stations near the airport

cityTips: Download offline maps of Puerto Vallarta in Google Maps before you arrive — cell service can be spotty between the Hotel Zone and Zona Romántica, and you will need navigation to compare taxi quotes with actual distances

The safest neighborhoods for tourists are Zona Romántica, Marina Vallarta, Centro, and the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) — avoid venturing into inland colonias after dark, and stick to well-lit streets even in tourist areas late at night

Carry a photocopy of your passport and leave the original in your hotel safe — Puerto Vallarta's US Consular Agency in Nuevo Vallarta is only open Monday through Thursday mornings, so losing your passport on a Friday means waiting until the following week for a replacement

Drink only bottled or purified water, including when brushing your teeth — most hotels and restaurants in the tourist zones use purified water and ice, but street food vendors and smaller establishments outside the main zones may not

faq.question: Is Puerto Vallarta safe for tourists in 2026?
faq.answer: Puerto Vallarta is widely considered one of the safest tourist destinations in Mexico. It has never received a specific 'Do Not Travel' advisory from the US State Department, though the broader state of Jalisco carries a Level 2 'Exercise Increased Caution' warning. The tourist zones — Zona Romántica, the Malecón, Marina Vallarta, Centro, and the Hotel Zone — are well-patrolled and active well into the evening. Violent crime affecting tourists is rare; the primary risks are petty theft, timeshare fraud, taxi overcharging, and ATM skimming. Puerto Vallarta attracted over 6 million visitors in 2023 with the vast majority having incident-free trips.

faq.question: Should I use Uber or taxis in Puerto Vallarta?
faq.answer: Both work, but each has trade-offs. Uber operates in Puerto Vallarta and is generally cheaper — a ride from the airport to the Zona Romántica costs around 150-200 pesos on Uber versus 350+ pesos in a taxi. However, the local taxi union has pushed back against Uber, and some drivers cancel rides near taxi stands to avoid confrontation. Taxis are plentiful but have no meters, so you must negotiate the fare before getting in. Ask your hotel for a printed zone rate card so you know the correct price. For airport transfers specifically, buying an official prepaid taxi voucher inside the terminal is the safest option.

faq.question: Is it safe to walk the Malecón at night?
faq.answer: Yes, the Malecón boardwalk is generally safe at night and is one of the liveliest areas in Puerto Vallarta after dark, with street performers, restaurants, and families walking well past midnight during peak season. However, you should be alert for pickpockets and the mustard distraction scam, keep your phone in a secure pocket rather than your hand, and avoid walking alone on the darker stretches south of the Rio Cuale bridge or north past the cruise terminal. Stick to the main lit boardwalk and you will be fine.

faq.question: What should I do if I get pressured into a timeshare presentation?
faq.answer: If you signed a contract, Mexican consumer protection law (Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor) gives you 5 business days to cancel any timeshare or vacation club purchase in writing. Send a cancellation letter via certified mail or email to the seller immediately and keep all documentation. If you are being pressured during a presentation, you can stand up and leave at any time — you are under no legal obligation to stay, regardless of what they tell you. If they physically prevent you from leaving, call 911. Report timeshare fraud to PROFECO at 800-468-8722 or file a complaint online at gob.mx/profeco. For US citizens, the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (ic3.gov) tracks Mexico-based timeshare fraud specifically.

faq.question: Is the tap water safe to drink in Puerto Vallarta?
faq.answer: No. Do not drink tap water in Puerto Vallarta. Stick to bottled water (agua embotellada), which is cheap and available everywhere — a 1.5-liter bottle costs about 15-20 pesos at OXXO. Most hotels and reputable restaurants in the tourist zones use purified water and purified ice (hielo purificado), so ice in your drinks at established restaurants is generally safe. Be more cautious at street food stands and smaller establishments outside the main tourist areas. Brush your teeth with bottled water to be safe, especially if you have a sensitive stomach.

police.name: Policía Municipal de Puerto Vallarta
police.notes: 911 is the universal emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance. The municipal police direct line is 322-224-8484. Bilingual Tourist Police can be reached at 329-291-6666.

consumerProtection.name: PROFECO (Federal Consumer Protection Agency)
consumerProtection.notes: Handles complaints about timeshare fraud, restaurant overcharging, taxi disputes, and vendor scams. Foreigners can file in English.

usConsulate.name: US Consular Agency Puerto Vallarta
usConsulate.address: Paseo de los Cocoteros #85, Sur Paradise Plaza Interior Local L-7, Nuevo Vallarta, Nayarit
usConsulate.notes: Closed weekends and US/Mexican holidays. For after-hours emergencies, call +1-202-501-4444.

emergencyContacts.lostPassport: File a police report immediately and contact the US Consular Agency in Nuevo Vallarta at +52-55-8526-2561 (Mon-Thu 8:30 AM-12:30 PM) or the 24/7 emergency line at +1-202-501-4444. Bring the police report, any photo ID, and two passport photos. Emergency passports are typically issued within 1-2 business days for approximately $150 USD. Keep a photocopy of your passport separately and store a digital scan in cloud storage before traveling.
